cards.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
cards.titleEn: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
cards.summary: Pope Leo had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said. Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican has said in a medical bulletin. The 71-year-old underwent a 90 minute surgery on Tuesday at Rome's Gemelli Hospital and was subsequently diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma. "After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room on the 10th floor," the Vatican said in a statement. The lump was first detected during what the Vatican has described as "routine checks".

cards.title: Albanian police fire tear gas at protesters as Education Ministry attacked
cards.titleEn: Albanian police fire tear gas at protesters as Education Ministry attacked
cards.summary: At least 23 protesters have been arrested in demonstrations in the capital. Albanian riot police have fired tear gas and water cannons at hundreds of student demonstrators protesting over education and social conditions in the capital Tirana. Protesters hurled bricks and concrete blocks at the Education Ministry on Tuesday, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. Student organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, financial support and employment prospects after graduation. At least six officers and one female journalist were injured, according to a statement by police, and 23 people were arrested.

cards.title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
cards.titleEn: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
cards.summary: The influential economics body has upgraded its UK growth forecast for this year, but risks remain. Countries around the world have had their future economic prospects assessed by influential body, the International Monetary Fund (IMF). What the IMF says matters – it aims to keep the global economy stable and its twice-yearly forecasts are one of the most authoritative looks at what is really going on around the world. Yet like all forecasts they can also turn out to be incorrect, so they shouldn't be treated as gospel. The transportation and production of energy in the Middle East has been severely disrupted, causing oil prices to jump and inflation to rise.

cards.title: More tea? How Scotland's crops of the future could be set to change
cards.titleEn: More tea? How Scotland's crops of the future could be set to change
cards.summary: Experts are examining the ways Scotland's farmers might diversify and adapt to a changing climate. Costing about £40 per packet for her most expensive product, it's not going to replace the supermarket brands any time soon. Droughts, intensive downpours and diseases have created challenges for tea growers across the world as they deal with the impact of a warming planet. But some experts believe Scotland's relatively settled climate could give the tea industry here a helping hand. As the picking season draws to a close, Susie plucks the last few leaves before proudly pouring me a small glass of her Kinnettles Gold, which is grown in a walled garden on the family farm near Forfar.

cards.title: (EDITORIAL from Korea JoongAng Daily on Oct. 14)
cards.titleEn: (EDITORIAL from Korea JoongAng Daily on Oct. 14)
cards.summary: Intelligence cooperation with Washington is in Korea's interest, not subservience: Ko... This will let Google show Yonhap news articles that match or are related to your search Korean Ambassador to the United States Kang Kyung-wha told a parliamentary audit Monday that intelligence cooperation is currently the most difficult issue in relations between Seoul and Washington. Recalling U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's remarks at a bilateral foreign ministers' meeting last month that there were problems with intelligence cooperation, Kang said she did not believe the situation had been sufficiently resolved to Washington's satisfaction. The dispute over restrictions on intelligence sharing has persisted for more than six months, following Unification Minister Chung Dong-young's remarks in March concerning a uranium enrichment facility in Kusong, North Pyongan Province.
